readings.summary: Implement the basic GeneratedMessagePackFormatter feature: generate a bodyless partial formatter class in Project B for a public-member type in Project A, defaulting to contractless behavior but honoring any MessagePack attributes already present on T.
readings.code_difference: The generator and new attribute need only support generation directly from T; no surrogate type, surrogate-property mapping, or other separate customization surface is required.

readings.summary: Implement the same formatter generation and also support the suggested optional SurrogateType property so callers in Project B can supply attribute/key settings through a surrogate type mapped to T's properties by name.
readings.code_difference: In addition to direct generation from T, the attribute must expose SurrogateType and the generator must read member/key settings from that surrogate and map them by property name to T, adding behavior and public API absent from the first reading.

data.quote: AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.
